articles.title: 15% decline in Indians seeking admission to UG courses in US: Report
articles.description: Amid the tightening of immigration policies, the number of Indian students seeking admission to US colleges declined by 15 per cent in 2025-26 over the previous year, according to a report. A report, representing over 1,100 institutions, released by the Common App, shows that although application volume for undergraduate admission in the upcoming 2026-27 academic year rose overall, the number of international applicants through March 1 fell 10 per cent, the steepest decline on record. The report by a non-profit organisation recorded a 15 per cent decrease in applicants from India -- the top source for international students in the US. India is the largest source of international students in the US, with over 3.63 lakh enrolling for different courses in the 2024-25 academic year. According to the report, international students contributed USD 41.77 billion to the local economy in the Fall 2025-26. The same number is projected to be 38.37 billion in 2026-27. articles.title: BIG! Russia Destroyed Major NATO Arms Factories? Explosive New ‘Covert War’ Details Emerge
articles.description: Russia's alleged shadow war in Europe may be moving closer to the heart of Ukraine's military supply chain. Western intelligence assessments reportedly point to a covert network using local operatives to target facilities linked to Ukraine's war effort, with arson and sabotage among the suspected tactics. Recent fires and explosions across several European countries are now drawing scrutiny, raising fresh questions over whether Moscow is testing a new way to hit Ukraine without triggering a direct NATO confrontation. However, Russian involvement has not been proven in every incident, and Moscow has repeatedly rejected such accusations. If the allegations are confirmed, Europe could be facing a quieter but increasingly dangerous front in the Russia-Ukraine war.

articles.description: Russia has issued a fresh warning over Britain’s continued military support for Ukraine, accusing London of actively contributing to the conflict and obstructing efforts toward a peaceful settlement. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Moscow views British involvement “extremely negatively,” while claiming that the UK is providing support connected to Ukraine’s production of SCALP missiles. Peskov warned that Russian forces are gathering intelligence on facilities involved in producing such weapons and other military equipment. He said Moscow is taking measures to destroy identified sites. The remarks come amid continued Western military assistance to Kyiv and growing tensions between Russia and the UK over weapons support and the broader course of the war.

articles.title: US launches ‘operation economic outcast’: Trump pressures world leaders to stop dealing with Iran?
articles.description: Donald Trump has launched what his administration calls an “economic D-Day” against Iran. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled Operation Economic Outcast, vowing to sever Tehran's financial lifelines worldwide and impose a “zero-leakage” sanctions campaign. Washington is targeting digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping while warning foreign governments and businesses against helping Iran. Bessent said Trump is personally calling world leaders and threatened to remove Iran-linked entities from the US dollar system. With dozens of targets already sanctioned, will Trump's financial offensive isolate Tehran or trigger another escalation?

articles.title: Putin turns Kim’s troops into new drone force for Ukraine? 400 N. Korean UAV operators reach Russia
articles.description: North Korea has reportedly deployed about 400 drone operators to Russia as part of an estimated 8,500-strong military contingent, deepening Pyongyang’s role in Moscow’s war effort. Ukrainian military intelligence says most of the force is in Russia’s Kursk region and includes roughly 1,000 engineers and deminers; the drone teams could conduct reconnaissance and strike missions against Ukraine from Russian territory. The claims have not been independently verified, but the deployment could give North Korean personnel crucial experience in modern drone warfare. It follows reports that Pyongyang was considering sending up to 25,000 workers to Russia’s Alabuga drone-production hub in exchange for drone-operations training.
